replaces.change: The bundled recipe pan-fried chicken in 25 g soy-sauce marinade and relied on 'cook until the chicken is cooked through'. Here the same peanut-lime idea bakes on one tray, soy drops to 1 tbsp tamari (gluten-free), the marinade is boiled before drizzling, and doneness is a thermometer check at 165°F. Sweet chili sauce replaced by the lime-honey balance in the marinade.

qty.note: gluten-free soy sauce - the bundled 25 g soy line, cut and converted

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a sheet pan with parchment. Cut the chicken into strips about 2 cm wide so they cook evenly.
Whisk the peanut butter, 3 tablespoons just-boiled water, tamari, honey, curry powder, garlic, ginger and oil into a pourable marinade - hot water thins the peanut butter without seizing it.
Toss the chicken strips in the marinade and let them sit while the oven finishes heating, at least 5 minutes.
Spread the strips out with space between them and bake for 10 to 12 minutes - they should take a light patchy brown at the edges.
Check the thickest strip with a thermometer: it must read 165°F (74°C), the FSIS safe minimum for poultry. Return to the oven in 2-minute bursts if it falls short.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: While the chicken rests, scrape any leftover marinade into a small pan and boil it hard for 2 full minutes - raw-marinade drips are not a sauce until they have boiled.
Cut the cucumber into fingers and dress them with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt at the table, not before - salted in advance they weep.
Serve the strips on the cucumber with the boiled marinade drizzled over and the remaining lime in wedges for zesting.

nutrition_per_serving.basis: USDA FoodData Central values committed in apps/ios/Resources/usda_ingredient_catalog.sqlite (matched fdc_id per ingredient in tables/nutrition-map.json), plus the app's shipped core-ingredient table (data.json) for items without an fdc_id; scaled by evidenced gram quantities
